_doc: The barkeep's mop (docs/briefs/mopping.md), a prop of kind mop (MopProp): an ash handle 1.3 m and 32 mm thick, and a head of cotton strands lashed to its foot as one soft body (the rag's parts). A cotton mop head of ~200 g holds about three times its weight of water and, pressed out, keeps about its own weight; past ~2.2 times it drips. Wet, it lifts dirt, spilt drink and blood off the boards it's dragged over (take_rate: the share of what's under it a second, dragged at a walking sweep); it leaves a thin film of its water, and with it a share of what it carries (a dirty mop spreads dirt). Rinsed in its bucket it gives up what it holds to the water and takes the bucket's back.
